name: empty
desc: Lightweight Expect-like PTY tool for shell scripts
why: An Expect-style PTY driver; a tidy way to script interactive programs and see what they really ask for.

brief.what_it_is: empty is a command-line utility that runs a program under a pseudo-terminal (PTY) session so a shell script can send it input and read its output. You invoke it from a shell prompt or inside a script, and it takes flags for input and output FIFOs, a wait-for-string mode, and a send mode, followed by the program to run. It is written entirely in C and does not depend on TCL, Perl, Python, or any other language runtime. The homepage presents it as a lightweight replacement for TCL/Expect.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says that one of the oldest problems in UNIX shell scripting is using command-line interactive programs from scripts, and the goal is to simplify managing interactive applications in plain sh scripts.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage gives an example in which empty -f -i in -o out telnet foo.bar.com starts telnet with named input and output pipes. Later calls use -w to wait for a prompt string on the output pipe and then send a reply, and -s to send a line of text. The page does not describe the internals beyond this.

commands_seen.context: Unpacks the downloaded source tarball; the homepage says installation is download, then ungzip and untar.

brief.install_notes: Download the source tarball from the homepage, unpack it, and run make with the target that matches your system (all install clean, or make `uname -s` ... variants on other UNIX systems). Installation places the binary and man page under /usr/local. The homepage does not mention a Homebrew formula or any runtime dependencies beyond a C compiler and make. Cygwin support is listed as experimental and points to a README.CYGWIN file.
brief.standout: It is a small C tool that gives shell scripts the Expect-style job of driving interactive programs, with no embedded scripting language. The homepage side-by-side shows the same telnet login as a shell script, a TCL/Expect script, a Perl Expect module script, and a Python pexpect script.
brief.status: Unknown. The homepage footer reads Copyright (C), 2005-2020 Mikhail E. Zakharov, which is the newest date visible. No release version, release date, or commit history appears on the page, and the page does not say the project is maintained or abandoned. The download link was not resolved to a repository, so I could not check.
brief.caveats: The homepage lists platforms where it was compiled and tested, including FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD, macOS, Linux, Solaris, AIX, HP-UX, and OSF1. The Cygwin port is marked experimental. The build relies on make targets that vary by system, and the page warns: Good luck and beware of bugs! The homepage gives no license text. Hosting is on SourceForge, and the page is old-style HTML.
quotes: empty is an utility that provides an interface to execute and/or interact with processes under pseudo-terminal sessions (PTYs).
In some cases empty can be the simplest replacement for TCL/expect or other similar programming tools
does not use TCL, Perl, PHP, Python or anything else as an underlying language
